rules.message: Chrome without its sandbox: a renderer exploit then runs code in the container (decision SEC-24).
rules.fix: Run Chrome as a non-root user (USER $APP_UID) with the sandbox on, and give the container a seccomp profile that allows clone, clone3 and unshare. An opt-out needs an ADR and trusted templates only.

rules.message: Chrome is downloaded at runtime: each container downloads it over the network, the start is slow, and the build is not pinned.
rules.fix: Install chrome-headless-shell at image build time, pinned to Chrome.DefaultBuildId, and set ExecutablePath or PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH.
match: await new BrowserFetcher(new BrowserFetcherOptions { Browser = SupportedBrowser.Chrome }).DownloadAsync();

rules.message: A visible browser or DevTools: this works only on a developer machine and opens a debug port.
rules.fix: Use HeadlessMode = HeadlessMode.Shell (or True) outside a developer machine, and no Devtools.

rules.message: A new browser for each call: a launch costs 1 to 2 seconds and a process tree, and parallel calls can exhaust memory.
rules.fix: Keep one browser per process in a singleton, a context and a page per render, and a SemaphoreSlim limit.
match: await using var browser = await Puppeteer.LaunchAsync(options);
using var browser = await Puppeteer.LaunchAsync(new LaunchOptions { Headless = true });
nomatch: await using var page = await context.NewPageAsync();

rules.message: PdfAsync writes a file: extra disk I/O, and a file stays behind when the process stops.
match: await page.PdfAsync(tempPath, new PdfOptions { Format = PaperFormat.A4 });
nomatch: await using var stream = await page.PdfStreamAsync(options);

match: var options = new LaunchOptions { HeadlessMode = HeadlessMode.Shell };
nomatch: await using var page = await context.NewPageAsync();
